```{r compute, cache=TRUE}
# same data, seeds, and settings as the Wednesday demos in CODE_Week10_ModelComparison.R
library(emdbook)
library(MASS)
library(glmnet)
library(cmdstanr)
library(loo)

fir <- na.omit(FirDBHFec[, c("TOTCONES", "DBH", "WAVE_NON")])
fir$TOTCONES <- round(fir$TOTCONES)
wave <- as.numeric(fir$WAVE_NON)
nll_nb <- function(a, b, k) -sum(dnbinom(fir$TOTCONES, mu = a * fir$DBH^b, size = k, log = TRUE))
fit_ml <- function(nll, start) {
  fit <- optim(start, nll, control = list(maxit = 10000))
  optim(fit$par, nll, method = "BFGS", control = list(maxit = 10000))
}
aic_nowave <- 2 * fit_ml(function(p) nll_nb(p[1], p[2], p[3]), c(1, 2, 1))$value + 6
aic_full <- 2 * fit_ml(function(p) nll_nb(p[1:2][wave], p[3:4][wave], p[5:6][wave]),
                       c(1, 1, 2, 2, 1, 1))$value + 12

fir_code <- "
data {
  int<lower=1> N;
  int<lower=1> G;
  array[N] int<lower=0> cones;
  vector<lower=0>[N] dbh;
  array[N] int<lower=1, upper=G> grp;
}
parameters {
  vector[G] log_a;
  vector[G] b;
  vector<lower=0>[G] k;
}
model {
  log_a ~ normal(0, 5);
  b ~ normal(0, 5);
  k ~ exponential(0.1);
  cones ~ neg_binomial_2(exp(log_a[grp]) .* pow(dbh, b[grp]), k[grp]);
}
generated quantities {
  vector[N] log_lik;
  for (i in 1:N)
    log_lik[i] = neg_binomial_2_lpmf(cones[i] | exp(log_a[grp[i]]) * dbh[i]^b[grp[i]], k[grp[i]]);
}
"
fir_model <- cmdstan_model(write_stan_file(fir_code))
fit_fir <- function(G) {
  grp <- if (G == 1) rep(1L, nrow(fir)) else wave
  fir_model$sample(data = list(N = nrow(fir), G = G, cones = fir$TOTCONES, dbh = fir$DBH,
                               grp = grp),
                   chains = 4, parallel_chains = 4, seed = 746, refresh = 0,
                   show_messages = FALSE)
}
fit_nowave_b <- fit_fir(1)
fit_full_b <- fit_fir(2)
dic <- function(fit, G) {
  grp <- if (G == 1) rep(1L, nrow(fir)) else wave
  d_bar <- mean(-2 * rowSums(fit$draws("log_lik", format = "matrix")))
  pm <- function(v) colMeans(fit$draws(v, format = "matrix"))
  d_hat <- -2 * sum(dnbinom(fir$TOTCONES, mu = exp(pm("log_a")[grp]) * fir$DBH^pm("b")[grp],
                            size = pm("k")[grp], log = TRUE))
  c(DIC = d_hat + 2 * (d_bar - d_hat), pD = d_bar - d_hat)
}
dic_nw <- dic(fit_nowave_b, 1)
dic_full <- dic(fit_full_b, 2)
waic_nw <- waic(fit_nowave_b$draws("log_lik", format = "matrix"))
waic_full <- waic(fit_full_b$draws("log_lik", format = "matrix"))
loo_nw <- fit_nowave_b$loo()
loo_full <- fit_full_b$loo()
fir_comp <- loo_compare(list(no_wave = loo_nw, full = loo_full))

covars <- c("canopy", "big_trees", "snags", "shrub", "elev", "slope",
            "north", "road_dist", "stream_dist", "grazing")
beta_true <- c(0, 0.5, 0.4, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0.3, 0, 0)
cov_mat <- diag(10)
cov_mat[1, 2] <- cov_mat[2, 1] <- 0.6
cov_mat[1, 4] <- cov_mat[4, 1] <- -0.4
cov_mat[5, 6] <- cov_mat[6, 5] <- 0.5
set.seed(19)
X <- mvrnorm(50, rep(0, 10), cov_mat)
colnames(X) <- covars
creepers <- rpois(50, exp(log(2) + X %*% beta_true))
set.seed(746)
cv_lasso <- cv.glmnet(X, creepers, family = "poisson", alpha = 1)
coef_lasso <- coef(cv_lasso, s = "lambda.1se")[-1]

pois_code <- "
data {
  int<lower=1> N;
  int<lower=1> K;
  matrix[N, K] X;
  array[N] int<lower=0> y;
  int<lower=1, upper=2> prior;
  real<lower=0> s;
}
parameters {
  real b0;
  vector[K] beta;
}
model {
  b0 ~ normal(0, 5);
  if (prior == 1) beta ~ normal(0, s);
  else beta ~ double_exponential(0, s);
  y ~ poisson_log(b0 + X * beta);
}
generated quantities {
  vector[N] log_lik;
  for (i in 1:N) log_lik[i] = poisson_log_lpmf(y[i] | b0 + X[i] * beta);
}
"
pois_model <- cmdstan_model(write_stan_file(pois_code))
fit_creepers <- function(prior, s) {
  pois_model$sample(data = list(N = 50, K = 10, X = X, y = creepers, prior = prior, s = s),
                    chains = 4, parallel_chains = 4, seed = 746, refresh = 0,
                    show_messages = FALSE)
}
fits_shrink <- list(vague = fit_creepers(1, 10), normal = fit_creepers(1, 0.2),
                    laplace = fit_creepers(2, 0.15))
post_sum <- lapply(fits_shrink, function(f) {
  as.matrix(f$summary("beta", "median", ~quantile(.x, c(0.05, 0.95)))[, -1])
})
loos_shrink <- lapply(fits_shrink, function(f) f$loo())
p_loo_shrink <- sapply(loos_shrink, function(l) l$estimates["p_loo", 1])
n_high_k <- sapply(loos_shrink, function(l) sum(l$diagnostics$pareto_k > 0.7))
shrink_comp <- loo_compare(loos_shrink)
```

```{r helpers}
f1 <- function(v) formatC(v, format = "f", digits = 1)
f2 <- function(v) formatC(round(v, 2) + 0, format = "f", digits = 2)

ic_tab <- data.frame(
  criterion = c("AIC", "DIC", "WAIC", "LOOIC"),
  no_wave = c(aic_nowave, dic_nw["DIC"], waic_nw$estimates["waic", 1], loo_nw$estimates["looic", 1]),
  full = c(aic_full, dic_full["DIC"], waic_full$estimates["waic", 1], loo_full$estimates["looic", 1]),
  penalty = c("k = 3 vs. 6",
              paste0("pD = ", f1(dic_nw["pD"]), " vs. ", f1(dic_full["pD"])),
              paste0("p_waic = ", f1(waic_nw$estimates["p_waic", 1]), " vs. ",
                     f1(waic_full$estimates["p_waic", 1])),
              paste0("p_loo = ", f1(loo_nw$estimates["p_loo", 1]), " vs. ",
                     f1(loo_full$estimates["p_loo", 1]))))
show_ic <- function() {
  out <- ic_tab
  out$penalty <- gsub("_", "\\\\_", out$penalty)
  knitr::kable(out, format = "latex", booktabs = TRUE, escape = FALSE, digits = 1,
               col.names = c("", "no wave", "full", "effective parameters"))
}

# posterior medians and 90% intervals under three priors, with truth and glmnet lasso
draw_intervals <- function() {
  par(mar = c(3.4, 6.5, 0.5, 0.5), mgp = c(2, 0.6, 0))
  plot(NA, xlim = c(-0.5, 1), ylim = c(0.5, 10.5), yaxt = "n", xlab = "Slope (per SD)", ylab = "")
  axis(2, at = 10:1, labels = gsub("_", " ", covars), las = 1, cex.axis = 0.8)
  abline(v = 0, col = "grey70")
  offsets <- c(vague = 0.25, normal = 0, laplace = -0.25)
  shades <- c(vague = "grey60", normal = "black", laplace = "black")
  pchs <- c(vague = 21, normal = 19, laplace = 17)
  for (p in names(post_sum)) {
    yy <- (10:1) + offsets[p]
    segments(post_sum[[p]][, 2], yy, post_sum[[p]][, 3], yy, lwd = 2, col = shades[p])
    points(post_sum[[p]][, 1], yy, pch = pchs[p], col = shades[p], bg = "white")
  }
  points(beta_true, 10:1, pch = 4, cex = 1.3, lwd = 2)
  legend("bottomright", c("vague prior", "Normal(0, 0.2)", "Laplace(0, 0.15)", "truth"),
         col = c("grey60", "black", "black", "black"), pch = c(21, 19, 17, 4),
         pt.bg = "white", bty = "n", cex = 0.75)
}

# prior shapes; the horseshoe is simulated (Normal with a half-Cauchy scale)
draw_priors <- function() {
  set.seed(746)
  hs <- rnorm(1e6, 0, 0.1 * abs(rcauchy(1e6)))
  par(mar = c(3.4, 3.4, 0.5, 0.5), mgp = c(2, 0.6, 0))
  curve(dnorm(x, 0, 0.2), -1, 1, n = 501, lwd = 2, ylim = c(0, 6),
        xlab = "Slope", ylab = "Prior density")
  curve(dexp(abs(x), 1 / 0.15) / 2, -1, 1, n = 501, add = TRUE, lwd = 2, lty = 2)
  lines(density(hs[abs(hs) < 1], bw = 0.01, n = 1024), lwd = 2, col = "grey55")
  legend("topright", c("Normal (ridge)", "Laplace (lasso)", "horseshoe"),
         lty = c(1, 2, 1), col = c("black", "black", "grey55"), lwd = 2, bty = "n", cex = 0.8)
}

nd <- function(m) fir_comp[m, ]
north_lap <- post_sum$laplace[7, ]
north_vague <- post_sum$vague[7, ]
```

# How to prepare (for students)

- **Big picture.** Monday compared models with likelihood ratio tests,
  AIC, and penalties on coefficient size (ridge, lasso). Today: the
  Bayesian versions. How do we compare models fit by MCMC, where there
  is no single best-fit parameter set, and how do priors do the job of
  a penalty?
- **Read:** Hooten and Hobbs (2015), *A guide to Bayesian model
  selection for ecologists* (Ecological Monographs 85: 3-28), the
  sections "Model validation," "Statistical regularization and
  information criteria," and "Guidance"; skim the rest. Bolker 6.6.3
  (printed p. 280-284) on Bayes factors and DIC.
- **Review:** Bayes' rule for parameters (posterior $\propto$ likelihood
  $\times$ prior); Monday's ridge and lasso penalties; fitting a model
  with `cmdstanr` (last week's take-home).

# Part 1: Lecture content

## 1. Big picture (~3 min) [BOARD]

- COMPARE (2), Bayesian side. Monday: penalties on count and size.
  Today: the same two ideas for MCMC fits
- No single $\hat\theta$ $\Rightarrow$ no AIC; priors blur "number of
  parameters"

## 2. WOD reveal (~10 min) [handout]

- $-\log P(\mu \mid y) = \sum (y_i - \mu)^2/(2\sigma^2) + \mu^2/(2\tau^2)$,
  so $\lambda = 1/(2\tau^2)$
- Ridge estimate = posterior mode; vague prior ($\tau \to \infty$) = MLE
- Lasso $\lambda|\mu|$ = Laplace prior: spike at 0, heavier tails

## 3. WAIC and LOO (~12 min) [BOARD $\to$ R]

- Score = **elpd**: for each data point, log of its likelihood averaged
  over the posterior; sum. Higher is better; IC $= -2 \times$ elpd
- Penalty = effective parameters, estimated from the posterior:
  - DIC (Bolker): $p_D$ = mean deviance $-$ deviance at posterior means
  - WAIC: $p_{waic}$ = summed posterior variance of each point's log lik.
  - LOO: approximates refitting without each point (PSIS); Pareto
    $k > 0.7$ flags points where the shortcut fails
- Stan must save `log_lik[i]` per observation (generated quantities)

```{r ic-table}
show_ic()
```

- Fir: elpd difference `r f1(nd("full")["elpd_diff"])` (SE
  `r f1(nd("full")["se_diff"])`); all Pareto $k$ good
- **Pause:** full model `r f1(-nd("full")["elpd_diff"])` behind, SE
  `r f1(nd("full")["se_diff"])`. Conclusion? *Land:* about one SE; can't
  tell the models apart (not "no wave effect")
- **Sticking point:** AIC gives no SE for a difference; LOO does

## 4. Shrinkage priors (~12 min) [BOARD $\to$ R]

- Prior scale plays $\lambda$'s role: Normal = ridge, Laplace = lasso
- Creepers (Monday), three priors on the 10 slopes:

```{r intervals-fig, fig.width=5.5, fig.height=3.6}
draw_intervals()
```

- Northness (truth 0): vague `r f2(north_vague[1])`
  (`r f2(north_vague[2])` to `r f2(north_vague[3])`); Laplace
  `r f2(north_lap[1])` (`r f2(north_lap[2])` to `r f2(north_lap[3])`)
- $p_{loo}$: vague `r f1(p_loo_shrink["vague"])`, Normal
  `r f1(p_loo_shrink["normal"])`, Laplace `r f1(p_loo_shrink["laplace"])`
  (10 slopes + intercept): tighter priors, fewer effective parameters
- LOO best: `r rownames(shrink_comp)[1]`; others within
  `r f1(max(-shrink_comp[, "elpd_diff"]))` elpd (SE up to
  `r f1(max(shrink_comp[, "se_diff"]))`). `r max(n_high_k)` stations
  have $k > 0.7$ (mention only)
- **Pause:** the lasso set northness to exactly 0; the Laplace
  posterior says `r f2(north_lap[1])` (`r f2(north_lap[2])` to
  `r f2(north_lap[3])`). Which is more honest? *Land:* the posterior
  keeps the uncertainty; a Bayesian lasso never gives exact zeros
- Horseshoe: tall spike plus heavy tails (small effects shrink hard,
  big ones barely). Sketch only:

```{r priors-fig, fig.width=4.5, fig.height=2.6}
draw_priors()
```

- **Sticking point:** choosing the prior scale = choosing $\lambda$;
  compare by LOO, or estimate it (a hierarchical prior, later)

## 5. Discussion (~5 min) [BOARD]

**Q1.** LOO prefers the no-wave fir model by
`r f1(-nd("full")["elpd_diff"])` elpd (SE `r f1(nd("full")["se_diff"])`).
A colleague writes "wave regeneration has no effect on cone
production." Agree?

**Q2.** With a Laplace prior, northness gets a posterior median of
`r f2(north_lap[1])` (90% interval `r f2(north_lap[2])` to
`r f2(north_lap[3])`); Monday's lasso said exactly 0. Which would you
report, and why?

- Q1 lands on: a difference within ~1 SE is inconclusive; "not
  detected" $\neq$ "no effect"; corroborated, not proven
- Q2 lands on: the posterior shows the uncertainty a single zero hides;
  for prediction either works, for inference report the interval

## If time: Bayes factors and selection inside the sampler [BOARD]

- Bayes factor = ratio of marginal likelihoods (averaged over the
  prior); sensitive to vague priors, hard to compute (Bolker 6.6.3)
- RJMCMC / spike-and-slab: the sampler jumps between models; posterior
  model probabilities. Needs discrete parameters, so not Stan (JAGS,
  NIMBLE); legacy LECTURE8 has BUGS code

# PART 2: PODIUM CHEAT SHEET

\normalsize
\textit{Terse on purpose. Detail: Part 1. R = Wednesday section of CODE\_Week10\_ModelComparison.R.}
\large

**Big picture $\to$ WOD $\to$ lecture. Take-home WOD out at end. Behind? Skip DIC; sec. 4 plot + pause only.**

## 1. Big picture (~3 min) [BOARD]

- COMPARE (2), Bayesian side
- Monday: count and size penalties. Today: both for MCMC fits
- No $\hat\theta$, fuzzy $k$ $\Rightarrow$ no AIC

\newpage

## 2. WOD reveal (~10 min)

- $-\log$ post. $= \sum (y_i - \mu)^2/(2\sigma^2) + \mu^2/(2\tau^2)$
- $\lambda = 1/(2\tau^2)$; ridge = posterior mode; $\tau \to \infty$ = MLE
- Lasso = Laplace prior

\newpage

## 3. WAIC and LOO (~12 min) [BOARD $\to$ R]

- elpd: per point, log of posterior-averaged lik.; sum
- $p_D$, $p_{waic}$, $p_{loo}$: effective parameters
- LOO = PSIS refit shortcut; Pareto $k > 0.7$ = unreliable
- Stan saves `log_lik[i]`

```{r podium-ic}
show_ic()
```

- **Pause:** full `r f1(-nd("full")["elpd_diff"])` behind, SE `r f1(nd("full")["se_diff"])`? About 1 SE: can't tell apart
- AIC: no SE. LOO: SE

\newpage

## 4. Shrinkage priors (~12 min) [BOARD $\to$ R]

```{r podium-intervals, fig.width=5.5, fig.height=3.4}
draw_intervals()
```

- Prior scale = $\lambda$; Normal = ridge, Laplace = lasso
- North: vague `r f2(north_vague[1])`, Laplace `r f2(north_lap[1])`
- $p_{loo}$: `r f1(p_loo_shrink["vague"])` $\to$ `r f1(p_loo_shrink["normal"])` $\to$ `r f1(p_loo_shrink["laplace"])`
- **Pause:** lasso 0 vs. Laplace `r f2(north_lap[1])` (`r f2(north_lap[2])`, `r f2(north_lap[3])`)? Posterior keeps uncertainty
- Horseshoe: spike + heavy tails (sketch)
- Prior scale = $\lambda$: LOO, or hierarchical later

\newpage

## 5. Discussion (~5 min)

**Q1.** No-wave fir model ahead by `r f1(-nd("full")["elpd_diff"])` elpd (SE `r f1(nd("full")["se_diff"])`). "Wave has no effect"?

- Inconclusive; not detected $\neq$ no effect

**Q2.** Northness: Laplace `r f2(north_lap[1])` (`r f2(north_lap[2])` to `r f2(north_lap[3])`) vs. lasso 0. Report which?

- Posterior shows the uncertainty a zero hides

**If time:** Bayes factors (marginal lik., prior-sensitive); RJMCMC / spike-and-slab (not Stan)
